answers.value: All application source repositories in the org's GitHub Enterprise 'abc-eng' organization for the service being changed; scope = every branch that has an open PR plus the default branch (main). Third-party libraries in scope via SCA on the resolved dependency manifest (package-lock.json/pom.xml).
Per pull request (blocking) and on the nightly full-repo scan at 02:00 ET; findings window = the current sprint for triage.

SAST scan (SonarQube + CodeQL) and SCA (Dependabot/Snyk) both execute and publish results to the PR check; SARIF report attached to the GitHub Actions run. Gate: 0 critical and 0 high findings; <=5 medium permitted only with a logged waiver.

Number of files/lines scanned in the SonarQube run reconciles to the git diff line count for the PR (delta scan) or full LOC for nightly; quality-gate summary shows 100% of changed files analyzed with 0 skipped.
SARIF + SonarQube analysis report retained as a GitHub Actions build artifact keyed to the commit SHA and PR number, retention 400 days; report timestamp and scanner version recorded.

Each accepted medium/low finding logged as a Jira issue type 'SDLC-Exception' with owner = Engineering Manager, risk rationale, and a 10-business-day remediation SLA; critical/high block the merge and cannot be waived.

answers.value: The full SIT+SysTest cycle for release candidate build tagged in the release pipeline; scope = all integration test suites plus end-to-end system scenarios covering the Guidewire PolicyCenter/ClaimCenter integration surface for the release under test.
Executed once per release candidate in the SIT environment; regression subset runs nightly. Cycle window = 3 business days from RC freeze to sign-off.
Every planned test case has a recorded status (Pass/Fail/Blocked) in the test management tool; 100% executed, 0 in 'Not Run' at cycle close; each failure linked to a defect.
Executed count reconciles to planned count in the test plan (planned = executed + explicitly deferred with approval); pass rate >= 98% and 0 open critical/blocker defects at sign-off.
Test execution report (JUnit XML + summary) archived as a Jenkins build artifact keyed to the RC build number, retained 400 days; each run stamped with build SHA, environment, and timestamp.

Failed cases raise a Jira defect (type 'Bug', linked to the test case); blockers gate the release. Any deferred case requires a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' with Test Lead + Product Owner approval and a target fix release.

checklist.step: SIT cycle sits at the integration/system layer above unit tests
checklist.value: Test plan maps cases to pyramid layers; integration+system suites cover cross-service flows not covered by unit tests, avoiding duplicate coverage.

testing.value: Coverage report shows unit > integration > E2E case counts; confirm no critical integration path relies solely on manual E2E.

checklist.step: Integration tests exercise external dependencies (Guidewire, IAM, messaging)

testing.value: Test report shows dedicated integration cases for each external system with pass status and captured request/response payloads.

checklist.value: SIT uses masked/synthetic data seeded from a versioned dataset; no production PII in SIT; data reset before each full cycle.

testing.value: Confirm the SIT dataset version is recorded in the run and a data-refresh job ran successfully before the cycle started.

checklist.step: Automated regression detection runs within the cycle

testing.value: Revert a fixed bug in a test branch; confirm the regression suite catches it and marks it as a regression against baseline.

answers.value: All new or materially changed system components in the current release for the service; scope = each component's API, data model, runbook, and README documentation requirements captured in Confluence space 'ENG-DOCS'.
Defined at design time per component and revalidated each release; requirements reviewed at the sprint design review.

Each component has a documentation requirement entry naming: doc type (README/OpenAPI/C4/runbook), owner, acceptance criteria, and target location; 100% of in-scope components have a filled entry, 0 marked TBD at design-review exit.
Count of documentation requirement entries reconciles to the count of new/changed components in the release manifest (1:1); design-review checklist shows no component without a doc requirement.
Requirements page versioned in Confluence with page history; each requirement linked to the Jira story and stamped with author + date.
Components with a justified documentation exception logged as Jira 'SDLC-Exception' with owner = Tech Lead and rationale; exceptions reviewed at the next architecture review.

Post-change: the Confluence doc-requirements page for the release lists every changed component present pre-change plus the new ones; diff of component list vs. release manifest = 0 unmatched entries.
Linked to the release change record in ServiceNow (CHG number) and the parent Jira epic for the release documentation work.
All new/changed components in the release (typically 8-15 per release); inspect each component's doc-requirement entry.
Pass = every component has a complete doc-requirement (type, owner, acceptance criteria, location) with no TBD; Fail if any component missing an entry or with placeholder text.
Missing or incomplete entries block design-review exit; a documented exception (Jira 'SDLC-Exception', Tech Lead owner) is the only path to proceed, with a deadline in the next sprint.
Component doc-requirement fields defined in the ENG-DOCS Confluence template: componentId, docType, owner, acceptanceCriteria, targetLocation, linkedJira.
Release manifest component count (source of truth = CI build's component inventory) used as the control total against doc-requirement entries.

Acceptance criteria: each in-scope component has an approved documentation requirement covering README, API spec, and runbook, with measurable done-criteria; evidence location = Confluence space ENG-DOCS, page 'Doc Requirements - <release>', linked from the release Jira epic.

answers.value: The automated regression suite for the service under test; scope = all critical user journeys and prior-defect regression cases for the application, wired to run in the CI pipeline on every merge to main and nightly.
Suite runs per pull request (smoke subset) and full nightly at 01:00 ET; baseline established at the start of the release train.

Suite is registered as a required CI stage; every case has an assertion and a stable selector/fixture; flaky-test quarantine < 2%. Coverage of critical paths >= 90%; changed-line unit coverage >= 80%.

Number of automated cases reconciles to the regression test inventory in the test-management tool (automated + manual-only = total); nightly run executes 100% of automated cases, 0 skipped without a quarantine tag.
JUnit XML results + HTML report retained as Jenkins artifacts per build (SHA-keyed), retention 400 days; trend dashboard stamps each run with timestamp and pass rate.

Failing regression case blocks the merge and opens a Jira 'Bug'; flaky cases moved to a quarantine tag with a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' (owner = QA Automation Engineer, 5-business-day fix SLA) and excluded from the gate until fixed.

checklist.step: All regression cases automated and integrated into CI
checklist.value: Regression inventory shows 100% of stable cases automated; manual retained only for exploratory; suite runs on every merge.

testing.value: Compare automated case count to total regression inventory; confirm >= 95% automated and CI trigger configured.

checklist.step: Suite detects regressions against a baseline

testing.value: Traceability matrix maps each critical path to at least one automated case; coverage metric >= 90%.

testing.value: Confirm the pipeline config invokes the suite and that a failing run prevents the deploy stage.

answers.value: All architecturally significant decisions for the service in the current quarter; scope = every ADR in the repo's docs/adr/ directory routed to the Architecture Review Board (ARB) and affected tech leads.

Template modules tagged in the platform git repo (semver); Backstage catalog entry stamped with version + owner; provisioning test results retained as CI artifacts (SHA-keyed, 400-day retention).

answers.value: All interface contracts between the integrated services in the release; scope = every OpenAPI/AsyncAPI contract and consumer-provider pact for the APIs owned or consumed by the service, validated in the CI contract-test stage.
Validated per pull request that touches an API/contract and on every release build; provider contract verification runs nightly against the current consumer pacts.
Every published contract validates against its schema; consumer pacts verify against the provider; 100% of contracts pass in CI; 0 breaking changes without a versioned contract and consumer sign-off.
Count of verified contracts in the Pact Broker reconciles to the service dependency map (every declared integration has a contract); 0 dependencies without a contract.
Pact verification results retained in the Pact Broker keyed to provider/consumer versions; CI logs (SHA-keyed) archived 400 days with timestamp and contract version.

A failed contract verification blocks the merge/deploy; a required breaking change follows the versioning + consumer-notification process and is logged as a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' (owner = Integration Architect) with a migration window.
Contract schema version (OpenAPI 3.x / AsyncAPI) is tagged and approved in the API catalog before publish; version recorded in the Pact Broker.

Contract validation is exact-match on required fields and types; optional-field additions are non-breaking, type/required changes are breaking (sensitivity = any change to required set or type triggers a version bump).
Materiality: any change affecting a live consumer's request/response contract is material and requires consumer sign-off; internal-only additive changes are immaterial.
Sample contract fields trace to the source API definition in the code (annotations/schema) and to the consumer's expected shape in the pact file.
Contract status in the Pact Broker (verified/unverified) aligns to the release gate; a contract must be 'verified' for its provider+consumer version pair before deploy.
Verification timestamps in the broker are within the current build window; stale verifications (older than the RC) are re-run before sign-off.
All provider-consumer contract pairs in the dependency map for the release (typically 6-20 pairs).
Pass = 100% of contract pairs verified green in the Pact Broker; Fail if any pair is red or unverified at release gate.
A red/unverified pair blocks deploy; breaking change requires versioned contract + consumer notification, tracked via Jira 'SDLC-Exception' (owner = Integration Architect).
Effective for the current release candidate; contract versions pinned to the RC tag; verification window = RC freeze to sign-off.

Source-system field definitions come from the provider's OpenAPI/AsyncAPI schema (single source of truth in the provider repo); control total = number of required fields per operation, reconciled between provider schema and consumer pact.

Approved contract version = the OpenAPI/AsyncAPI tag approved in the API catalog; parameter source = the provider's schema definition; both recorded against the Pact Broker verification for the release.

answers.value: The event streaming/messaging platform (Kafka/Azure Service Bus) for the enterprise integration estate; scope = all production topics, brokers, consumer groups, and schemas operated by the integration team, managed against defined SLOs.
Continuous operation; SLA/throughput reviewed monthly; capacity and retention config reviewed quarterly. Reporting window = rolling 30 days.

Every topic has an owner, schema (registered in the schema registry), retention, and partition config; broker health, consumer lag, and throughput dashboards live. SLO: 99.9% broker availability, p99 end-to-end latency < 500ms, consumer lag < 10k messages sustained.
Produced vs. consumed message counts reconcile per topic within tolerance (no unexplained drops); DLQ counts tracked and reconciled; topic inventory matches the CMDB/service catalog.
SLA/throughput reports exported monthly to the ITSM/observability platform with timestamp; config changes tracked via ServiceNow change records; dashboards snapshot retained per reporting period.

SLA breaches raise a ServiceNow incident with severity by impact; sustained lag or DLQ growth triggers the runbook and on-call; capacity exceptions logged as Jira 'SDLC-Exception' (owner = Platform Engineering Lead).

answers.value: The team's product backlog for the current planning cycle; scope = all ready backlog items in the Jira project being ranked via WSJF (or MoSCoW), covering the next 2-3 sprints of candidate work.

All 'Ready' backlog items in the planning cycle (typically 20-60 items).
